# Better analytical ideas, made tangible.

<p class="hero-lead">CentralStatz builds interactive prototypes for better ways to think, work, and make decisions with data.</p>

<p class="hero-support">Each project begins with a real analytical problem—not a technology demo. Rigorous reasoning defines the structure; rapid, AI-assisted development makes alternative ways of framing and solving it tangible early enough to test.</p>

<span class="section-index">03 / AI’s role</span>

## Faster implementation changes more than speed.

AI-assisted development can reduce the distance between a well-reasoned concept and a working interface. More importantly, lower implementation cost expands the set of solutions worth considering: alternative formulations, interactive assumptions, dynamic systems, and workflows that connect models to decisions can be tested before one structure becomes expensive to replace.

:::

::: {.ai-boundary}

### Acceleration

- analytical code, interfaces, and supporting workflows
- comparison of designs before committing
- creation of testable analytical artifacts
- iteration between reasoning and use

### Expanded possibility

- reconsider the shape and scope of the project
- represent decisions, states, uncertainty, or trajectories when useful
- compare meaningful analytical formulations
- let the problem determine the machinery

<p class="boundary-note">The goal is not maximum sophistication. It is less compromise for the wrong reasons. Statistical reasoning, domain expertise, validation, and judgment still determine what should be built.</p>

:::

:::

:::

<span class="section-index">04 / Philosophy</span>

## Structure Before Sophistication {#philosophy}

Sophisticated-looking outputs are becoming easier to generate. Framing, definitions, assumptions, architecture, and validation are not.

Poor thinking can now be implemented faster, too. Structure is the quality-control layer: the disciplined design that makes an analytical system transparent, reproducible, maintainable, and defensible.

Expanded technical capability does not make complexity inherently better. A simple method is still the right method when it matches the question, data, and decision. Structure decides where added machinery earns its place—and where it does not.

<div class="principle-grid">
  <div><strong>Clear questions</strong><span>Let the actual question—not inherited machinery—set the boundary.</span></div>
  <div><strong>Defensible logic</strong><span>Make metrics and assumptions open to review.</span></div>
  <div><strong>Reproducible systems</strong><span>Build work that can be understood and repeated.</span></div>
  <div><strong>Honest boundaries</strong><span>State uncertainty and limits alongside capability.</span></div>
</div>

:::

<span class="section-index">06 / About</span>

## A statistician’s lab for analytical systems. {#about}

CentralStatz was founded by **Alex Zajichek**, a statistician and data scientist in Central Wisconsin with more than a decade of experience learning, teaching, and doing data science work across tools, methods, and problem contexts.

His work is especially grounded in healthcare, where messy systems, consequential decisions, and fragile metrics make sound analytical structure essential. Through the lab, Alex explores, designs, prototypes, and evaluates systems that make complex analytical questions easier to engage with—and easier to scrutinize.

:::

```{=html}
<div id="submissionModal" class="modal" role="dialog" aria-modal="true" aria-labelledby="modalTitle" hidden>
  <div class="modal-content">
    <button type="button" class="close-modal" aria-label="Close dialog">&times;</button>
    <h3 id="modalTitle">What happens when I submit?</h3>
    <p>Your note goes directly to me at <a href="mailto:alex@centralstatz.com">alex@centralstatz.com</a>. I’ll review it and respond by email with any initial perspective I can offer. It is a connection point—not a commitment or obligation.</p>
    <p><strong>— Alex</strong></p>
  </div>
</div>
<script>
(() => {
  const modal = document.getElementById('submissionModal');
  const openButton = document.getElementById('openSubmissionModal');
  const closeButton = modal?.querySelector('.close-modal');
  let previousFocus;
  if (!modal || !openButton || !closeButton) return;
  const open = () => { previousFocus = document.activeElement; modal.hidden = false; document.body.classList.add('modal-open'); closeButton.focus(); };
  const close = () => { modal.hidden = true; document.body.classList.remove('modal-open'); previousFocus?.focus(); };
  openButton.addEventListener('click', open);
  closeButton.addEventListener('click', close);
  modal.addEventListener('click', event => { if (event.target === modal) close(); });
  document.addEventListener('keydown', event => { if (event.key === 'Escape' && !modal.hidden) close(); });
})();
</script>
```
